title: Take an HRESULT apart
description:
Write `decode(hr)`, which splits a 32-bit `HRESULT` value into its parts and returns them in an `HrParts`:

- `failed`: true if bit 31 is set;
- `facility`: bits 16 to 26 (11 bits);
- `code`: bits 0 to 15.

Then write `fromWin32(error)`, which builds the `HRESULT` that wraps a Win32 error code the way `HRESULT_FROM_WIN32` does: 0 stays 0 (success); anything else becomes failure, facility 7, and the low 16 bits of the error as the code.

```
decode(0x80070005)  ->  failed, facility 7, code 5
decode(0x00000001)  ->  not failed, facility 0, code 1
fromWin32(2)        ->  0x80070002
```

Work with the bits yourself: the Windows macros are not available here.
hints: To read a field, shift it down to bit 0 with `>>`, then keep only its width with `&`: 11 bits is `0x7FF`, 16 bits is `0xFFFF`.
To build one, shift each part up into place with `<<` and combine them with `|`.
lessonTitle: Errors, GetLastError and Reading the Documentation
